entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Bom dia!
entries.en: Good morning!

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Bom dia! Tudo bem?
entries.en: Good morning! How are you? (literally: everything well?)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Tudo bem, obrigado. E tu?
entries.en: I'm fine, thanks. And you? (informal tu)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Tudo ótimo!
entries.en: Everything's great!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Muito prazer!
entries.en: Nice to meet you!

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: O prazer é meu.
entries.en: The pleasure is mine.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: O meu nome é Kevin.
entries.en: My name is Kevin.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Muito prazer, Kevin. Eu sou a Ana.
entries.en: Nice to meet you, Kevin. I'm Ana.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Como está?
entries.en: How are you? (neutral/polite)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Estou bem, obrigada.
entries.en: I'm well, thank you (said by a woman).

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Quantas pessoas?
entries.en: How many people?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Duas pessoas.
entries.en: Two people.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Uma pessoa. Só eu.
entries.en: One person. Just me.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Mesa para quantos?
entries.en: Table for how many?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Para três, se faz favor.
entries.en: For three, please. (se faz favor = please, very Portuguese)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Quanto custa?
entries.en: How much does it cost?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Custa vinte euros.
entries.en: It costs twenty euros.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Um, dois, três, quatro, cinco.
entries.en: One, two, three, four, five.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Seis, sete, oito, nove, dez.
entries.en: Six, seven, eight, nine, ten.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Boa noite! Bem-vindo!
entries.en: Good evening! Welcome!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Boa noite! Tem mesa livre?
entries.en: Good evening! Do you have a free table?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Temos sim. Para quantas pessoas?
entries.en: Yes, we do. For how many people?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Para duas pessoas.
entries.en: For two people.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Por aqui, se faz favor.
entries.en: This way, please.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Quanto tempo de espera?
entries.en: How long is the wait?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Uns dez minutos.
entries.en: About ten minutes.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Está bem, nós esperamos.
entries.en: Okay, we'll wait.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Desculpe, estamos cheios neste momento.
entries.en: Sorry, we're full right now.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: O que deseja?
entries.en: What would you like? (classic waiter line)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Queria o prato do dia, se faz favor.
entries.en: I'd like the dish of the day, please. (queria = polite I'd like)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Para mim, o bitoque.
entries.en: For me, the bitoque (steak with egg and fries).

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Para beber?
entries.en: Anything to drink?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Uma água sem gás, se faz favor.
entries.en: A still water, please.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Mais alguma coisa?
entries.en: Anything else?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Não, só isso. Obrigado.
entries.en: No, that's all. Thank you.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: A conta, se faz favor.
entries.en: The bill, please.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Como deseja pagar?
entries.en: How would you like to pay?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Posso pagar com cartão?
entries.en: Can I pay by card?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Bom dia! Diga-me.
entries.en: Good morning! Tell me. (typical café greeting)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Um café, se faz favor.
entries.en: An espresso, please.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Com açúcar?
entries.en: With sugar?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Sem açúcar, obrigado.
entries.en: Without sugar, thanks.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Uma bica e um pastel de nata, se faz favor.
entries.en: A bica (Lisbon espresso) and a custard tart, please.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Quer o pastel quente, com canela?
entries.en: Do you want the tart warm, with cinnamon?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Quero sim! Adoro pastel de nata.
entries.en: Yes, please! I love pastel de nata.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: É para cá ou para levar?
entries.en: Is it for here or to go?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Para levar, se faz favor.
entries.en: To go, please.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Boa tarde! Posso ajudar?
entries.en: Good afternoon! Can I help you?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Tenho uma reserva. O meu nome é Kevin Jackson.
entries.en: I have a reservation. My name is Kevin Jackson.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Deixe-me ver... Sim, encontrei. Quarto para duas noites.
entries.en: Let me see... Yes, I found it. Room for two nights.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Ótimo. A que horas é o pequeno-almoço?
entries.en: Great. What time is breakfast? (pequeno-almoço = breakfast)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Das sete às dez e meia da manhã.
entries.en: From seven to ten thirty in the morning.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: O quarto tem Wi-Fi?
entries.en: Does the room have Wi-Fi?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Tem sim. A palavra-passe está no cartão.
entries.en: Yes, it does. The password is on the card. (palavra-passe = password)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Obrigado. Em que andar fica o quarto?
entries.en: Thank you. What floor is the room on?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: No terceiro andar. O elevador é ali.
entries.en: On the third floor. The elevator is over there.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Com licença, táxi!
entries.en: Excuse me, taxi!

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Boa tarde. Para onde?
entries.en: Good afternoon. Where to?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Para o aeroporto, se faz favor.
entries.en: To the airport, please.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Quanto tempo demora daqui até lá?
entries.en: How long does it take from here to there? (demorar = to take time)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Uns trinta minutos, dependendo do trânsito.
entries.en: About thirty minutes, depending on traffic.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Está bem. Tenho pressa.
entries.en: Okay. I'm in a hurry. (Portugal: ter pressa, not estar com pressa)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Chegámos. São vinte e cinco euros.
entries.en: We've arrived. That's twenty-five euros.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Pode ficar com o troco.
entries.en: Keep the change.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Obrigado! Boa viagem!
entries.en: Thank you! Have a good trip!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Com licença. Onde fica a estação de metro?
entries.en: Excuse me. Where is the metro station?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Fica a cinco minutos daqui, sempre em frente.
entries.en: It's five minutes from here, straight ahead.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Como é que eu chego lá?
entries.en: How do I get there?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Siga em frente e vire à direita no semáforo.
entries.en: Go straight and turn right at the traffic light. (formal imperative)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: É longe daqui?
entries.en: Is it far from here?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Não, é mesmo perto. Dois minutos a pé.
entries.en: No, it's really close. Two minutes on foot.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Há uma casa de banho por aqui?
entries.en: Is there a bathroom around here? (casa de banho = bathroom)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Há, ali na esquina.
entries.en: Yes, there on the corner.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Muito obrigado pela ajuda!
entries.en: Thank you very much for the help!

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Posso ajudar?
entries.en: Can I help you?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Estou só a ver, obrigado.
entries.en: I'm just looking, thanks. (estar a + infinitive = European progressive)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Quanto é isto?
entries.en: How much is this?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Esse custa cinquenta euros.
entries.en: That one costs fifty euros.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Tem um tamanho maior?
entries.en: Do you have a bigger size?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Temos sim. Quer experimentar?
entries.en: Yes, we do. Do you want to try it on?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Onde fica o provador?
entries.en: Where is the fitting room?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Está muito caro. Faz algum desconto?
entries.en: It's too expensive. Can you do a discount?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: A pronto pagamento tem dez por cento de desconto.
entries.en: Cash payment has ten percent off. (a pronto = cash)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Fico com ele!
entries.en: I'll take it! (literally: I stay with it — the classic way to buy)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Temos promoção! Bananas a dois euros o quilo!
entries.en: We've got a deal! Bananas two euros a kilo!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Dê-me um quilo de bananas, se faz favor.
entries.en: Give me a kilo of bananas, please. (dê-me = give me, formal imperative)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Este ananás está maduro?
entries.en: Is this pineapple ripe? (ananás = pineapple in Portugal)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Está sim, senhor. Docinho!
entries.en: Yes sir. Nice and sweet!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: A quanto está o quilo do tomate?
entries.en: How much is a kilo of tomatoes?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: A seis euros o quilo.
entries.en: Six euros a kilo.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Faz-me por cinco?
entries.en: Can you do it for five for me?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Para o senhor, faço!
entries.en: For you, sir, I'll do it!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Obrigado! Até à próxima!
entries.en: Thanks! See you next time!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Como está o tempo hoje?
entries.en: How is the weather today?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Está imenso sol!
entries.en: It's super sunny!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: A água está fria?
entries.en: Is the water cold?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Não, está uma maravilha!
entries.en: No, it's wonderful!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Onde posso alugar uma espreguiçadeira?
entries.en: Where can I rent a sun lounger? (espreguiçadeira = sun lounger)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Ali no bar amarelo.
entries.en: There at the yellow beach bar.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Um sumo de laranja natural, se faz favor.
entries.en: A fresh orange juice, please. (sumo = juice)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Com ou sem gelo?
entries.en: With or without ice?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Com bastante gelo!
entries.en: With plenty of ice!

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: O que é que vais fazer amanhã?
entries.en: What are you going to do tomorrow? (informal tu)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Vou visitar a Torre de Belém.
entries.en: I'm going to visit the Belém Tower.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: No fim de semana vou para a praia.
entries.en: On the weekend I'm going to the beach.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Que giro! Queres companhia?
entries.en: How cool! Do you want company?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Claro! Vamos juntos.
entries.en: Of course! Let's go together.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: A que horas vais sair?
entries.en: What time are you going to leave?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Vou sair às oito da manhã.
entries.en: I'm going to leave at eight in the morning.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Vais de carro ou de autocarro?
entries.en: Are you going by car or by bus? (autocarro = bus)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Vou de metro. É mais rápido.
entries.en: I'm going by metro. It's faster.

title: Day 13 — Small Talk: Where Are You From

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: És daqui?
entries.en: Are you from here? (informal tu)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Não, sou dos Estados Unidos.
entries.en: No, I'm from the United States.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: A sério? De que cidade?
entries.en: Really? From which city?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Sou de Mesa, no Arizona. E tu?
entries.en: I'm from Mesa, in Arizona. And you?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Eu sou de Lisboa.
entries.en: I'm from Lisbon.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: É a primeira vez em Portugal?
entries.en: Is it your first time in Portugal?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Não, é a segunda vez. Adoro Portugal.
entries.en: No, it's the second time. I love Portugal.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Falas português muito bem!
entries.en: You speak Portuguese very well!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Obrigado! Ainda estou a aprender.
entries.en: Thank you! I'm still learning.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Desculpe, não percebi.
entries.en: Sorry, I didn't understand. (perceber = to understand)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Pode repetir, se faz favor?
entries.en: Can you repeat, please?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Pode falar mais devagar?
entries.en: Can you speak more slowly?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Claro, sem problema.
entries.en: Of course, no problem.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: O que significa esta palavra?
entries.en: What does this word mean?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Significa 'thank you' em inglês.
entries.en: It means 'thank you' in English.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Como se diz 'water' em português?
entries.en: How do you say 'water' in Portuguese?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Diz-se 'água'.
entries.en: You say 'água'.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Fala inglês?
entries.en: Do you speak English?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Falo um bocadinho.
entries.en: I speak a tiny bit. (bocadinho = little bit)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Tudo bem contigo?
entries.en: Is everything good with you? (contigo = with you, informal)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Tudo ótimo! Estou a adorar Portugal.
entries.en: Everything's great! I'm loving Portugal.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Onde queres almoçar hoje?
entries.en: Where do you want to have lunch today?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Quero comer um bacalhau à Brás de verdade.
entries.en: I want to eat a proper bacalhau à Brás (codfish dish).

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Conheço um sítio perfeito!
entries.en: I know a perfect place! (sítio = place)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Depois vamos tomar um café?
entries.en: Afterwards shall we have a coffee?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Boa ideia! Estás a falar cada vez melhor.
entries.en: Good idea! You're speaking better and better.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Obrigado! Estou a praticar todos os dias.
entries.en: Thanks! I'm practicing every day.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Passaporte, se faz favor.
entries.en: Passport, please.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Aqui está.
entries.en: Here it is.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Qual é o motivo da sua viagem?
entries.en: What is the reason for your trip?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Turismo. Vou ficar duas semanas.
entries.en: Tourism. I'm going to stay two weeks.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Onde é que vai ficar hospedado?
entries.en: Where will you be staying?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: No hotel Avenida Palace, em Lisboa.
entries.en: At the Avenida Palace hotel, in Lisbon.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Está tudo certo. Bem-vindo a Portugal!
entries.en: All good. Welcome to Portugal!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Obrigado! Onde levanto a minha bagagem?
entries.en: Thank you! Where do I pick up my luggage? (levantar = to pick up)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: No tapete número três, à direita.
entries.en: At carousel number three, to the right. (tapete = carousel belt)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Boa noite! Mesa para quantos?
entries.en: Good evening! Table for how many?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Para dois, se faz favor.
entries.en: For two, please.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Aqui está a ementa.
entries.en: Here is the menu. (ementa = menu)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: O que recomenda?
entries.en: What do you recommend?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: O bacalhau à Brás é o prato da casa.
entries.en: The bacalhau à Brás is the house specialty.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Perfeito. Um bacalhau à Brás e dois sumos de maracujá.
entries.en: Perfect. One bacalhau à Brás and two passion fruit juices.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Excelente escolha. Já venho.
entries.en: Excellent choice. Be right back.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Estava delicioso! A conta, se faz favor.
entries.en: It was delicious! The bill, please.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: São trinta e oito euros.
entries.en: That's thirty-eight euros.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Posso pagar com MB Way?
entries.en: Can I pay with MB Way? (the Portuguese payment app)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Pode sim! O número está aqui.
entries.en: Yes you can! The number is here.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Boa noite. Tenho uma reserva em nome de Jackson.
entries.en: Good evening. I have a reservation under Jackson.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Um momento... Encontrei. Três noites, com pequeno-almoço incluído.
entries.en: One moment... Found it. Three nights, breakfast included.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Isso mesmo. Posso fazer o check-in agora?
entries.en: That's right. Can I check in now?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Claro. Preciso de um documento de identificação.
entries.en: Of course. I need an ID document.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Aqui está o meu passaporte.
entries.en: Here is my passport.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: O seu quarto é o quinhentos e dois, no quinto andar.
entries.en: Your room is five-oh-two, on the fifth floor.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: O checkout é a que horas?
entries.en: What time is checkout?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Ao meio-dia. Bom descanso!
entries.en: At noon. Rest well!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Bom dia! Para a Avenida da Liberdade, se faz favor.
entries.en: Good morning! To Avenida da Liberdade, please.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Claro. Quer ir pela Segunda Circular? É mais rápido.
entries.en: Sure. Do you want to go via the Segunda Circular? It's faster. (Lisbon expressway)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Quanto tempo demora?
entries.en: How long does it take?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Vinte minutos, mais ou menos.
entries.en: Twenty minutes, more or less.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Perfeito, tenho pressa para uma reunião.
entries.en: Perfect, I'm in a hurry for a meeting.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Chegámos. Dezoito euros.
entries.en: We've arrived. Eighteen euros.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Aqui está. Pode ficar com o troco.
entries.en: Here you go. Keep the change.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Obrigado! Boa reunião!
entries.en: Thank you! Have a good meeting!

title: Day 1 — Ser vs Estar in Real Life

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: És americano?
entries.en: Are you American? (permanent characteristic — ser; informal tu)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Sou sim. Sou do Arizona.
entries.en: Yes I am. I'm from Arizona.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: E estás a gostar de Portugal?
entries.en: And are you enjoying Portugal? (estar a + infinitive = European progressive)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Estou a adorar! Estou muito feliz aqui.
entries.en: I'm loving it! I'm very happy here.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Como é a tua cidade?
entries.en: What is your city like?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: É quente e seca, como o Alentejo.
entries.en: It's hot and dry, like the Alentejo.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Estás cansado da viagem?
entries.en: Are you tired from the trip?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Estou um bocado, mas estou entusiasmado.
entries.en: I am a bit, but I'm excited. (bocado = a bit)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Bom dia. Tenho dores de cabeça.
entries.en: Good morning. I have a headache.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Há quanto tempo se sente assim?
entries.en: How long have you been feeling like this?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Desde ontem à noite.
entries.en: Since last night.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Tem alergia a algum medicamento?
entries.en: Are you allergic to any medication? (medicamento = medicine)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Não, não tenho.
entries.en: No, I'm not.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Tome um comprimido de oito em oito horas.
entries.en: Take one pill every eight hours.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Precisa de receita médica?
entries.en: Does it need a prescription?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Não precisa. Vende-se sem receita.
entries.en: It doesn't. It's sold without a prescription.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Também tenho dores de garganta.
entries.en: I have a sore throat too.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Leve estas pastilhas também. As melhoras!
entries.en: Take these lozenges too. Get well! (as melhoras = get well)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Está? Clínica Santa Maria, bom dia.
entries.en: Hello? Santa Maria clinic, good morning. (Está? = phone greeting)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Bom dia. Gostaria de marcar uma consulta.
entries.en: Good morning. I'd like to book an appointment.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Com que médico?
entries.en: With which doctor?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Com a doutora Fernanda, se for possível.
entries.en: With Doctor Fernanda, if possible.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Ela tem uma vaga na quinta-feira, às catorze horas.
entries.en: She has a slot on Thursday at 2 PM.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Perfeito. Pode marcar para mim, se faz favor?
entries.en: Perfect. Can you book it for me, please?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Qual é o seu nome completo?
entries.en: What is your full name?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Kevin Jackson. J-A-C-K-S-O-N.
entries.en: Kevin Jackson. J-A-C-K-S-O-N.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Está marcado. Quinta-feira às duas. Confirme um dia antes, se faz favor.
entries.en: Booked. Thursday at two. Please confirm one day before.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Olá! Como queres o corte hoje?
entries.en: Hi! How do you want the cut today?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Só um aparo, se faz favor. Nada muito curto.
entries.en: Just a trim, please. Nothing too short. (aparo = trim)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Máquina número dois dos lados?
entries.en: Number two clippers on the sides?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Isso. E em cima, só as pontas.
entries.en: That's it. And on top, just the ends.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Queres que eu faça a barba também?
entries.en: Do you want me to do your beard too?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Quero sim. Quanto fica tudo?
entries.en: Yes, please. How much is everything?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Corte e barba, vinte euros.
entries.en: Cut and beard, twenty euros.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Está bem. Obrigado!
entries.en: Great. Thank you!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Bom dia. Quero trocar dólares por euros.
entries.en: Good morning. I want to exchange dollars for euros.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Qual é o montante?
entries.en: How much? (montante = amount)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Trezentos dólares. Qual é o câmbio hoje?
entries.en: Three hundred dollars. What's the exchange rate today? (câmbio = rate)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Está a um euro e dez hoje.
entries.en: It's one euro ten today.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Tem comissão de serviço?
entries.en: Is there a service fee? (comissão = fee)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Tem, cinco euros por operação.
entries.en: Yes, five euros per transaction.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Onde há um Multibanco?
entries.en: Where is there an ATM? (Multibanco = the Portuguese ATM network)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Lá fora, do lado direito.
entries.en: Outside, on the right side.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: O MB Way funciona para estrangeiros?
entries.en: Does MB Way work for foreigners?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Funciona com conta portuguesa.
entries.en: It works with a Portuguese account.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Estás a procurar apartamento?
entries.en: Are you looking for an apartment?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Estou sim. Quero um sítio perto do metro.
entries.en: I am. I want a place near the metro.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: De quantos quartos?
entries.en: With how many bedrooms?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Um quarto chega. É só para mim.
entries.en: One bedroom is enough. It's just for me. (chegar = to be enough)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Qual é o teu orçamento?
entries.en: What is your budget?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Até oitocentos euros por mês, com condomínio incluído.
entries.en: Up to eight hundred euros a month, including building fees.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: O bairro é seguro?
entries.en: Is the neighborhood safe?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: É tranquilo. Tem uma pastelaria e um minimercado na esquina.
entries.en: It's calm. There's a pastry shop and a mini-market on the corner.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: O que é que fazes?
entries.en: What do you do? (work)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Trabalho em tecnologia. Sou gestor de projetos.
entries.en: I work in tech. I'm a project manager. (gestor = manager)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Que interessante! Trabalhas nisso há quanto tempo?
entries.en: How interesting! How long have you worked in that?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Há mais de dez anos.
entries.en: For more than ten years.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Trabalhas remotamente ou no escritório?
entries.en: Do you work remotely or at the office?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Híbrido. Três dias em casa, dois no escritório.
entries.en: Hybrid. Three days at home, two at the office.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Gostas do teu trabalho?
entries.en: Do you like your job?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Gosto muito. A minha equipa é ótima — tem gente de Tóquio.
entries.en: I like it a lot. My team is great — there are people from Tokyo. (equipa = team)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Queres sair para jantar sexta-feira?
entries.en: Do you want to go out for dinner on Friday?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Adorava! A que horas?
entries.en: I'd love to! At what time?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Às oito. Conheces aquele restaurante em Alfama?
entries.en: At eight. Do you know that restaurant in Alfama?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Conheço! É ótimo. Quem mais vai?
entries.en: I do! It's great. Who else is going?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: A Juliana e o Marcos. Vou enviar a localização.
entries.en: Juliana and Marcos. I'll send the location.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Infelizmente não posso na sexta. Pode ser no sábado?
entries.en: Unfortunately I can't on Friday. Can it be Saturday?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Pode sim! Sábado então, à mesma hora.
entries.en: Yes it can! Saturday then, same time.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Gostas de música portuguesa?
entries.en: Do you like Portuguese music?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Adoro! Gosto muito de fado.
entries.en: I love it! I really like fado. (Portugal's soul music)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: E kizomba? Gostas de dançar?
entries.en: And kizomba? Do you like to dance? (hugely popular in Portugal)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Gosto, mas danço muito mal!
entries.en: I do, but I dance very badly!

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: O que é que não gostas de fazer?
entries.en: What do you not like doing?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Não gosto de acordar cedo, mas estou a habituar-me.
entries.en: I don't like waking up early, but I'm getting used to it. (habituar-me = European clitic placement)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Qual é a tua comida portuguesa favorita?
entries.en: What is your favorite Portuguese food?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Bacalhau à Brás, sem dúvida. E pastel de nata, claro.
entries.en: Bacalhau à Brás, no doubt. And pastel de nata, of course.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: O que é que fizeste no fim de semana?
entries.en: What did you do on the weekend? (fizeste = tu preterite)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Fui à praia no sábado e descansei no domingo.
entries.en: I went to the beach on Saturday and rested on Sunday.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Que fixe! Com quem foste?
entries.en: Nice! Who did you go with? (fixe = cool, everyday slang)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Fui com uns amigos portugueses. Comemos peixe grelhado à beira-mar.
entries.en: I went with some Portuguese friends. We ate grilled fish by the sea.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Já experimentaste ginjinha?
entries.en: Have you tried ginjinha yet? (Lisbon's cherry liqueur)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Já! Experimentei ontem. É forte!
entries.en: I have! I tried it yesterday. It's strong!

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Gostaste?
entries.en: Did you like it?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Gostei muito, mas só bebi uma.
entries.en: I liked it a lot, but I only had one.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: A que horas acordas normalmente?
entries.en: What time do you normally wake up?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Acordo às seis e meia, tomo o pequeno-almoço e começo a trabalhar.
entries.en: I wake up at six thirty, have breakfast and start working.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Costumas fazer exercício de manhã?
entries.en: Do you usually exercise in the morning? (costumar = to usually do)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Faço exercício três vezes por semana. Corro no parque.
entries.en: I exercise three times a week. I run in the park.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: E à noite, o que é que fazes?
entries.en: And at night, what do you do?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Cozinho, estudo português um bocado e deito-me cedo.
entries.en: I cook, study Portuguese a bit and go to bed early. (deitar-se = to go to bed)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Estás a adaptar-te bem ao fuso horário?
entries.en: Are you adapting well to the time zone?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Estou a adaptar-me devagar. Ainda acordo de madrugada às vezes.
entries.en: I'm adapting slowly. I still wake up in the middle of the night sometimes.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Como foi a tua semana?
entries.en: How was your week?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Foi uma correria, mas boa. Trabalhei muito e estudei todos os dias.
entries.en: It was a rush, but good. I worked a lot and studied every day.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Já marcaste a consulta que precisavas?
entries.en: Did you already book the appointment you needed?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Marquei sim. Liguei ontem e consegui uma vaga.
entries.en: I did. I called yesterday and got a slot.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: O teu português melhorou imenso este mês!
entries.en: Your Portuguese improved so much this month! (imenso = hugely)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Obrigado! Agora consigo resolver quase tudo sozinho.
entries.en: Thank you! Now I can handle almost everything by myself.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Boa tarde. O que é que sente?
entries.en: Good afternoon. What are you feeling?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Tenho febre e dores no corpo desde ontem.
entries.en: I've had a fever and body aches since yesterday.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Tem dor de garganta ou tosse?
entries.en: Do you have a sore throat or cough?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Um bocado de tosse seca.
entries.en: A bit of a dry cough.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Vou examiná-lo. Respire fundo, se faz favor.
entries.en: I'm going to examine you. Take a deep breath, please. (examiná-lo = examine you, European clitic)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: É algo sério, doutora?
entries.en: Is it something serious, doctor?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Não, é só uma gripe ligeira. Repouso e muitos líquidos.
entries.en: No, it's just a mild flu. Rest and lots of fluids.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Preciso de voltar aqui?
entries.en: Do I need to come back?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Só se a febre não passar em três dias.
entries.en: Only if the fever doesn't go away in three days.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Está? Cabeleireiro Estrela.
entries.en: Hello? Estrela hair salon.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Olá, bom dia. Queria marcar para amanhã.
entries.en: Hi, good morning. I'd like to book for tomorrow.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Temos às dez ou às quinze horas. Qual prefere?
entries.en: We have ten or three PM. Which do you prefer?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Às dez, se faz favor. Em nome de Kevin.
entries.en: At ten, please. Under Kevin.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Anotado. Corte e barba?
entries.en: Noted. Cut and beard?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Só corte desta vez. Muito obrigado!
entries.en: Just a cut this time. Thank you very much!

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Nós agradecemos! Até amanhã.
entries.en: Thank you! See you tomorrow.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Tu és o Kevin, certo? Bem-vindo à equipa!
entries.en: You're Kevin, right? Welcome to the team!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Isso! Muito prazer. Estou entusiasmado para trabalhar convosco.
entries.en: That's me! Nice to meet you. I'm excited to work with you all. (convosco = with you all)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Onde trabalhavas antes?
entries.en: Where did you work before?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Trabalhava numa empresa de tecnologia americana, remotamente.
entries.en: I worked at an American tech company, remotely.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: E o que é que achas de trabalhar com uma equipa portuguesa?
entries.en: And what do you think about working with a Portuguese team?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Estou a adorar. Quero aprender mais sobre a cultura daqui.
entries.en: I'm loving it. I want to learn more about the culture here.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Sexta há um convívio com a equipa. Vens?
entries.en: Friday there's a get-together with the team. Are you coming? (convívio = social gathering)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Com certeza! Onde vai ser?
entries.en: Definitely! Where will it be?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Então pá, tudo fixe?
entries.en: Hey man, all good? (pá = dude; fixe = cool/fine — everyday Portuguese slang)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Tudo fixe! E contigo, tudo bem?
entries.en: All good! And with you, everything alright?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Tudo porreiro! Tens andado desaparecido!
entries.en: All great! You've been missing in action! (porreiro = cool)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Pois é, 'tava uma correria no trabalho.
entries.en: Yeah, work was a real rush. ('tava = estava, casual)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Deixa lá, 'bora tomar um café qualquer dia.
entries.en: Never mind, let's grab a coffee sometime. (deixa lá = never mind)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: 'Bora! Manda-me mensagem no WhatsApp.
entries.en: Let's! Send me a message on WhatsApp.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Combinado! Obrigado, pá!
entries.en: Done! Thanks, man! (combinado = agreed)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Fica bem! Até já!
entries.en: Take care! See you soon! (fica bem = take care)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: O que é que achaste do jogo ontem?
entries.en: What did you think of the game yesterday?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Acho que Portugal jogou muito mal.
entries.en: I think Portugal played very badly. (acho que = I think)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Discordo. Na minha opinião, a equipa esteve bem.
entries.en: I disagree. In my opinion, the team did well. (equipa = team)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Para mim, o problema foi a defesa.
entries.en: For me, the problem was the defense.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Pode ser. Mas o ataque também não ajudou.
entries.en: Maybe. But the attack didn't help either.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Concordo contigo nessa parte.
entries.en: I agree with you on that part.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: E o selecionador? Achas que ele fica?
entries.en: And the national coach? Do you think he stays? (selecionador = national team coach)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Duvido. Acho que o vão despedir.
entries.en: I doubt it. I think they'll fire him.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Conta lá! O que é que aconteceu no fim de semana?
entries.en: Tell me! What happened on the weekend? (conta lá = tell me)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Fui a um aniversário de um amigo. Foi muito giro.
entries.en: I went to a friend's birthday. It was really nice. (giro = cool/nice)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Havia muita gente?
entries.en: Were there a lot of people?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Havia umas trinta pessoas. Comemos grelhados a tarde toda.
entries.en: There were about thirty people. We ate grilled food all afternoon.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: E domingo, o que é que fizeste?
entries.en: And Sunday, what did you do?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Dormi até tarde e fiquei em casa a ver séries.
entries.en: I slept in and stayed home watching series.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Merecias, depois de uma semana daquelas.
entries.en: You deserved it, after that kind of week.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Vamos sair hoje à noite?
entries.en: Shall we go out tonight?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Vamos! Tens algum sítio em mente?
entries.en: Let's! Do you have somewhere in mind?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: 'Tou a pensar naquele bar com música ao vivo.
entries.en: I'm thinking about that bar with live music. ('tou = estou, casual)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: A que horas queres ir?
entries.en: What time do you want to go?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Às nove? Passo aí para te ir buscar.
entries.en: At nine? I'll come by to pick you up. (ir buscar = to pick up)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Combinado. Posso levar a minha prima?
entries.en: Agreed. Can I bring my cousin?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Claro! Quanta mais gente, melhor.
entries.en: Of course! The more people, the better.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Então, andas a sair com alguém?
entries.en: So, are you seeing anyone? (andar a + inf = to be doing regularly)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: 'Tou a conhecer uma pessoa. Ainda é cedo.
entries.en: I'm getting to know someone. It's still early.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Onde é que se conheceram?
entries.en: Where did you two meet?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Num curso de português. Ela é portuguesa.
entries.en: In a Portuguese course. She's Portuguese.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Que fofo! E já saíram?
entries.en: How cute! And have you gone out yet?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Já. Fomos jantar no sábado. Foi muito bom.
entries.en: We have. We went to dinner on Saturday. It was really good.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Vai haver um segundo encontro?
entries.en: Will there be a second date?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Espero que sim! Ela é muito fixe.
entries.en: I hope so! She's really cool.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Boa noite, senhora. Muito prazer em conhecê-la.
entries.en: Good evening, ma'am. Very nice to meet you. (formal; conhecê-la = meet you)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: O prazer é meu, Kevin. Entra, está à vontade!
entries.en: The pleasure is mine, Kevin. Come in, make yourself at home!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: A sua casa é linda. Obrigado pelo convite.
entries.en: Your home is beautiful. Thank you for the invitation.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: A Juliana fala muito bem de ti.
entries.en: Juliana speaks very well of you.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Fico contente. Ela é uma pessoa muito especial.
entries.en: I'm glad. She's a very special person. (ficar contente = to be glad)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Queres jantar connosco? Fiz uma lasanha.
entries.en: Do you want to have dinner with us? I made lasagna. (connosco = with us)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Adorava, muito obrigado. Cheira muito bem!
entries.en: I'd love to, thank you very much. It smells great!

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Não vais acreditar no que me aconteceu!
entries.en: You're not going to believe what happened to me!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Conta lá! Estou curioso.
entries.en: Tell me! I'm curious.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Eu 'tava no metro e, de repente, começou a chover a potes.
entries.en: I was on the metro and, suddenly, it started pouring rain. (chover a potes = to pour)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Nossa! E depois, o que é que fizeste?
entries.en: Wow! And then what did you do?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Corri para uma pastelaria e fiquei lá uma hora à espera.
entries.en: I ran to a pastry shop and stayed there an hour waiting.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Que doideira! Pelo menos havia café.
entries.en: That's crazy! At least there was coffee. (doideira = craziness)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: É, no fim de contas até foi bom.
entries.en: Yeah, in the end it was actually fine.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Quais são os teus planos para o próximo ano?
entries.en: What are your plans for next year?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Espero voltar a Portugal mais duas vezes.
entries.en: I hope to come back to Portugal two more times. (espero + infinitive)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Tomara que dê certo!
entries.en: I hope it works out!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Espero que o meu português melhore até lá.
entries.en: I hope my Portuguese improves by then. (subjunctive)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Vai melhorar de certeza. Praticas todos os dias.
entries.en: It will improve for sure. You practice every day.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Gostava de morar aqui um tempo, quem sabe um dia.
entries.en: I'd like to live here for a while, maybe someday. (gostava = I'd like)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Seria incrível! Já és quase português.
entries.en: It would be amazing! You're almost Portuguese already.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Que tipo de música ouves?
entries.en: What kind of music do you listen to?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Um bocado de tudo. Em Portugal, fiquei viciado em fado.
entries.en: A bit of everything. In Portugal, I got hooked on fado.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: A sério? De que fadista gostas mais?
entries.en: Really? Which fado singer do you like the most?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Gosto muito de uma que um amigo me mostrou. E tu, o que recomendas?
entries.en: I really like one a friend showed me. And you, what do you recommend?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Ouve Amália Rodrigues. Ela é um clássico.
entries.en: Listen to Amália Rodrigues. She's a classic. (the queen of fado)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Vou ouvir hoje à noite. Manda-me o nome da música.
entries.en: I'll listen tonight. Send me the song name.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Já viste telenovelas portuguesas?
entries.en: Have you seen Portuguese soap operas?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Comecei a ver uma esta semana. É ótima para treinar o ouvido.
entries.en: I started watching one this week. It's great for training my ear.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Então, conta-me as novidades!
entries.en: So, tell me the news!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Muita coisa boa. O trabalho vai bem e o meu português está a fluir.
entries.en: Lots of good things. Work is going well and my Portuguese is flowing.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Notei! Estás a falar tal e qual um português.
entries.en: I noticed! You're speaking just like a Portuguese person. (tal e qual = exactly like)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Muito obrigado! Ainda erro bastante, mas já não tenho medo de errar.
entries.en: Thank you so much! I still make mistakes, but I'm not afraid of making them anymore.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Esse é o segredo. E os planos para o próximo mês?
entries.en: That's the secret. And plans for next month?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Vou viajar para o Algarve com a Juliana. Vai ser a minha primeira vez lá.
entries.en: I'm traveling to the Algarve with Juliana. It'll be my first time there.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Vais adorar. Manda-me fotos!
entries.en: You're going to love it. Send me photos!

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Podes crer! Vamos combinar um jantar quando eu voltar.
entries.en: You bet! Let's plan a dinner when I get back. (podes crer = you bet, slang)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Ó Kevin! Chegaste! Queres uma cerveja?
entries.en: Hey Kevin! You made it! Want a beer?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Boas! Aceito sim. Os grelhados têm ótimo aspeto.
entries.en: Hey! I'll take one. The grilled food looks great. (boas = casual hi; aspeto = look)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: O Marcos é o mestre da grelha oficial do grupo.
entries.en: Marcos is the official grill master of the group.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Posso ajudar com alguma coisa?
entries.en: Can I help with anything?

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Descontrai, tu és convidado. Aproveita!
entries.en: Relax, you're a guest. Just enjoy! (descontrai = relax, tu imperative)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: A carne está no ponto perfeito. Parabéns!
entries.en: The meat is perfectly cooked. Congrats!

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Obrigado! Serve-te de mais pão de alho.
entries.en: Thanks! Help yourself to more garlic bread. (serve-te = help yourself)

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Este é o melhor programa de domingo. Obrigado pelo convite, pessoal.
entries.en: This is the best Sunday plan. Thanks for the invite, everyone. (pessoal = everyone/guys)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Bem-vindo, Kevin! A Ana falou tanto de ti.
entries.en: Welcome, Kevin! Ana has told us so much about you.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Muito obrigado por me receberem. Trouxe uma sobremesa.
entries.en: Thank you so much for having me. I brought a dessert.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Que gentil! Não precisavas, a sério.
entries.en: How kind! You really didn't have to.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Faço questão. É um costume da minha família também.
entries.en: I insist. It's a custom in my family too. (fazer questão = to insist)

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: O teu português é muito bom! Onde aprendeste?
entries.en: Your Portuguese is very good! Where did you learn?

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Estudei sozinho e pratiquei muito com a Ana. Ela é uma ótima professora.
entries.en: I studied on my own and practiced a lot with Ana. She's a great teacher.

entries.speaker: P
entries.jp: Ela puxou à mãe, que também é professora.
entries.en: She takes after her mother, who is also a teacher.

entries.speaker: K
entries.jp: Vê-se de onde vem a paciência dela!
entries.en: You can tell where her patience comes from!
